hypothesis: Canonical run identity plus an exact failed-run artifact, authoritative pending-decomposition claim, exact source-content digest, and transition-stable task-contract digest will prevent forged or replayed failures while admitting only the production ready-to-doing task move.

metricsCompared.name: unbound failed-run sources reaching decomposition
metricsCompared.baseline: Trigger runDir and runId were accepted as arbitrary strings; metadata and artifact ownership were not authenticated; a newer builder claim was explicitly accepted during finalization.
metricsCompared.candidate: Canonical path, metadata identity, active pending-decomposition ownership, artifact equality, exact source bytes, and canonical-transition task-contract checks fail closed before planning and are repeated before apply.

metricsCompared.name: decomposer ownership regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: No regressions covered traversing sources, metadata forgery, missing claims, same-id task replacement, or pre-apply ownership change; one test allowed a newer builder run claim.
metricsCompared.candidate: The decomposer suite passes 40 tests, including a production claim writer plus canonical task mover regression that proves the inode changes; 18 focused claim tests and the shipped subprocess replay also pass.
metricsCompared.unit: focused security cases and passing decomposer tests

rationale: The candidate uses existing path-safe run validation, the canonical claim store, and no-follow task readers. Claims record exact source bytes plus a contract digest that omits only lifecycle frontmatter. Same-path tasks still require the original inode and exact bytes; moved tasks require canonical serialized content, the same contract digest, and exactly ready-to-doing. The production-writer/mover regression and replay prove the legitimate path without synthetic inode preservation. Focused tests, build, typecheck, workflow validation, and lint pass.
